title: The Fox and the Stork
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Fox invited a Stork to dinner, at which the only fare provided was a large flat dish of soup. The Fox lapped it up with great relish, but the Stork with her long bill tried in vain to partake of the savoury broth. Her evident distress caused the sly Fox much amusement. But not long after the Stork invited him in turn, and set before him a pitcher with a long and narrow neck, into which she could get her bill with ease. Thus, while she enjoyed her dinner, the Fox sat by hungry and helpless, for it was impossible for him to reach the tempting contents of the vessel.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Fox serve the Stork for dinner?
options: A pitcher of fresh milk
A basket of small fish
A large flat dish of soup
A bowl of grain and seeds

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why can't the Stork eat the soup at the Fox's dinner?
options: Her long bill cannot manage the flat, shallow dish
The soup is too hot for her to touch
The Fox eats it all before she arrives
She does not care for the taste of soup

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Fox react to the Stork's struggle with the soup?
options: He offers to feed her himself
He apologizes and fetches a different dish
He refuses to eat until she is served properly
He is much amused by her distress

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Stork serve the Fox when she invites him to dinner?
options: A large flat dish like the Fox used
A pitcher with a long and narrow neck
A basket woven from reeds
A wide, shallow bowl of broth

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is the Fox unable to do at the Stork's dinner?
options: Find his way to the Stork's home
Finish eating before the Stork does
Reach the contents of the pitcher
Recognize the food that is served

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Stork choose a pitcher with a long, narrow neck for her dinner?
options: It suits her own bill while shutting the Fox out, just as he had done to her
It is the only dish she owns
It keeps the food warmer for longer
It was a gift from the Fox himself

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Stork's choice of dish suggest about her feelings toward the Fox's earlier trick?
options: She has forgotten all about the first dinner
She wants to make peace by serving his favorite food
She is unaware that the Fox once mocked her
She is repaying him in kind for his amusement at her expense

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "fare" mean in "the only fare provided was a large flat dish of soup"?
options: The price charged for a meal
The food that is served
The distance travelled to arrive
The dishes used to serve a meal

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Fox lapped up the soup with "relish"?
options: With great caution
With visible embarrassment
With obvious enjoyment
With noisy complaint

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: A trick played on someone else may well be played back on you
Foxes and Storks should never share a meal together
Only the cleverest animal at a dinner can ever eat well
Soup is a poor choice of food for any dinner party

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who invites whom to dinner first?
options: The Stork invites the Fox
They arrange the first dinner together
Neither one issues an invitation
The Fox invites the Stork

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Fox eat the soup at his own dinner?
options: He pours it into a smaller cup
He laps it up with great relish
He waits until it cools before eating
He shares it evenly with the Stork

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happens to the Stork while the Fox goes hungry at her dinner?
options: She also fails to eat anything
She offers to share her food with him
She enjoys her dinner with ease
She apologizes for the narrow pitcher

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Stork wait until her own dinner to respond to the Fox's trick?
options: She needs the chance to serve a dish suited to her own bill instead of his
She is too polite to say anything at the first dinner
She does not realize the Fox has tricked her until much later
She wants to give the Fox a second chance to be kind

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the outcome of the second dinner suggest about the Fox's earlier amusement?
options: It permanently ends his friendship with the Stork
It teaches the Stork to avoid dinners altogether
It has no real consequence for him at all
It comes back to cost him a meal of his own

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Stork tried "in vain" to eat the soup?
options: She tried without being noticed
She tried without success
She tried eagerly and quickly
She tried only once before giving up

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: The Fox and the Stork share a meal that satisfies them both
The Stork refuses to ever dine with the Fox again
The Stork repays the Fox's trick with a dinner he cannot eat either
The Fox teaches the Stork how to eat from a flat dish
